summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted with chest pain and severe nausea and vomiting. Initial concerns for cardiac or pulmonary causes were ruled out with a normal EKG and chest X-ray. She developed coffee-ground emesis, suggesting upper gastrointestinal bleeding likely due to gastritis or a Mallory-Weiss tear, but declined endoscopy. Her symptoms were managed with IV fluids, antiemetics, acid suppression, and pain control. Anxiety and chronic back pain were also addressed during the admission. Her condition improved with supportive care, and she was transitioned from NPO to a regular diet. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume her usual medications and follow up with GI, endocrinology, and psychiatry.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, with hemorrhage
